recipes.title: Caprese salad (tomato, basil & mozzarella)
steps: Slice the tomatoes into rounds.
Lay them on a plate. Tuck basil leaves and cheese slices between them.
Drizzle with oil (and vinegar if you like). Sprinkle salt and pepper.
Eat right away while the tomatoes are room temperature.
recipes.storage: Best eaten fresh. Keep tomatoes on the counter, not in the fridge — cold makes them mealy.
recipes.variety: Big juicy slicers like Brandywine or Celebrity, or a mix of colorful cherry tomatoes.
recipes.kid: Kids can tear the basil and arrange the plate.

recipes.title: Gurkensalat (creamy German cucumber salad)
steps: Spread the cucumber and onion slices on a big plate. Salt both sides and let them sit 30 minutes.
Drain them in a colander and gently squeeze out the water.
Stir the sour cream, sugar, vinegar, dill and parsley in a big bowl. Fold in the cucumbers and onions.
Cover and chill at least 3 hours (overnight is fine). Sprinkle paprika on top.
recipes.storage: Keeps 1–2 days in the fridge (it gets watery — stir before serving).
recipes.variety: Thin-skinned slicers like Marketmore or Straight Eight; burpless types need no peeling.

recipes.title: Tabbouleh herb salad
steps: Cover the bulgur with hot water and let it soak 20 minutes. (Own wheat: crack it in a blender, then simmer 15 minutes.) Drain well.
Chop the parsley and mint very fine. Dice the tomato and cucumber small.
Mix everything with lemon juice, oil and salt.
Taste. It should be bright and lemony — add more lemon if needed.
recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days in the fridge. The herbs darken a little.
recipes.variety: Flat-leaf (Italian) parsley has the best flavor here.

recipes.title: Fattoush crunchy bread salad
steps: Tear the pita into bite-size pieces. Toast in a dry pan or oven until crisp.
Chop the vegetables into chunks. Slice the radishes thin.
Whisk oil, lemon, sumac and salt.
Toss the salad and dressing. Add the pita last so it stays crunchy.
recipes.storage: Dress only what you will eat. Undressed chopped vegetables keep 1 day.
recipes.variety: Crisp romaine or a butterhead lettuce; Cherry Belle or French Breakfast radishes.

Slice the strawberries.
Shake oil, vinegar, honey and salt in a jar.

recipes.title: Kale salad with balsamic dressing
steps: Toast the nuts in a dry pan, stirring, until light brown. Let them cool.
Cut out the tough middle rib of each kale leaf. Slice the leaves into thin ribbons.
Whisk balsamic, oil, rice vinegar, honey, salt and pepper.
Toss kale, nuts, cranberries and dressing 30 minutes to 2 hours before eating so the kale softens. Stir in the cheese right before serving.
recipes.storage: Dressed kale keeps 2 days in the fridge (add the cheese and nuts fresh).
recipes.variety: Lacinato (dinosaur) kale is tender; frost-kissed kale tastes sweeter.
recipes.kid: Massaging the kale is a great job for kids.

recipes.variety: Small, crunchy pickling or Asian cucumbers.

Boil them 5–7 minutes until just tender. Drain.
Mix lemon, oil, cumin, paprika, garlic and salt.
Toss with the warm carrots and herbs. Serve warm or cold.

recipes.variety: Danvers or Nantes carrots; stored fall carrots work great.

recipes.title: Warm bacon potato salad
steps: Cook the bacon until crisp. Cut it into small pieces.
Boil the potatoes until just soft. Cut them into chunks and let them cool to room temperature in a big bowl.
Mix flour, celery seed, parsley, onion, salt and pepper. Bring the water, vinegar and sugar to a boil, stir in the flour mix and stir until thick.
Pour the warm dressing over the potatoes and bacon. Stir in the chopped eggs. Sprinkle paprika on top.
recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days in the fridge. Warm it a little before serving.
recipes.variety: Waxy red or yellow potatoes (Red Norland, Yukon Gold) hold their shape.

steps: Rinse the wheat berries. Simmer them in plenty of salted water for about 1 hour, until chewy-tender. Drain and cool.
Chop the vegetables and herbs.
Mix oil, vinegar and salt.
Toss everything together. Taste and add salt.
recipes.storage: Keeps 5 days in the fridge. Cooked wheat berries also freeze well.
recipes.variety: Hard red or soft white wheat both work; use threshed, cleaned berries.

Cool, then rub off the skins with a paper towel. Cut into wedges.
Peel and slice the oranges.
Arrange beets and oranges on greens. Drizzle oil, vinegar and salt.
recipes.storage: Roasted beets keep 1 week in the fridge.
recipes.variety: Detroit Dark Red; golden beets will not stain everything pink.

Splash in soy sauce. Serve hot.

recipes.variety: Any stored fall roots — parsnips taste sweeter after frost.

recipes.title: Mexican street corn (elote)

Grill or broil the ears 8–10 minutes, turning, until spotted brown. Or boil 5 minutes.
Brush with mayo. Roll in cheese.
Sprinkle chili powder and cilantro. Squeeze lime on top.

recipes.variety: Super-sweet types like Bodacious or Incredible stay sweet longest after picking.

recipes.variety: Pick pods at 2–4 inches; Clemson Spineless is easy to handle.

Turn the heat low. Stir often for 30–40 minutes, until thick and creamy.
Stir in butter, cheese and herbs.

recipes.title: Zucchini fritters
steps: Grate the zucchini. Mix in 1 tsp salt and let it drain in a strainer for 10 minutes. Press out the water with a spoon, then squeeze it dry in a towel.
Make the dip: stir sour cream, garlic, half the lemon zest, the lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
In a big bowl whisk the egg. Add zucchini, flour, green onions, thyme, basil, the rest of the zest, 1 tsp salt and the pepper.
Heat the oil in a skillet until shimmery. Drop in spoonfuls, flatten a little, and fry 2–3 minutes per side until golden. Drain on paper towels and eat with the dip.
recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat in a pan or oven. Freezes 2 months.
recipes.variety: Any zucchini, even the one that got too big — scoop out big seeds first.

recipes.title: Eggplant parmesan
steps: Slice the eggplant 1/4–1/2 inch thick. Salt the slices and let them sit on a rack for 30–60 minutes to draw out water.
Make the sauce: cook garlic in a little oil for 1 minute, add the chopped tomatoes and simmer until thick. Stir in half the basil, salt and pepper.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Mix breadcrumbs with 1/4 cup parmesan. Dip each slice in flour, then egg, then crumbs. Lay them on oiled sheet pans and bake 18–20 minutes, flipping halfway.
Turn the oven to 350°F (175°C). In a baking dish layer sauce, eggplant, mozzarella, parmesan and basil; repeat. Bake 30–35 minutes until bubbly. Rest 10 minutes before cutting.
recipes.storage: Keeps 4 days in the fridge; freezes 3 months.
recipes.variety: Black Beauty or Rosa Bianca eggplant.

Cook the mushrooms in butter until soft; add garlic and thyme. Sprinkle in 2–3 Tbsp flour, then stir in half and half and broth until thick. Add parmesan and salt.
Stir in the beans, pour into a baking dish, top with the crispy onions and bake about 20 minutes until bubbly.
recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days in the fridge (onions soften).
recipes.variety: Tender snap beans like Provider or Blue Lake.

crops.amt: 2 lb, trimmed and cut in 2-inch pieces
2 Tbsp dried herbs for the onions

recipes.title: Sweet potato casserole with pecans
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Butter a 2-quart baking dish.
Peel the sweet potatoes, cut into 2-inch chunks and boil until very soft. Drain and blend or mash smooth.
Mix in milk, maple syrup, egg, 1/2 tsp cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, salt and orange zest. Spread in the dish.
Rub pecans, flour, brown sugar, butter and 1/2 tsp cinnamon into clumps, scatter on top, and bake 30–35 minutes until golden.
recipes.storage: Make the mash 2 days ahead; leftovers keep 4 days.
recipes.variety: Beauregard or Covington, cured 2 weeks for sweetness.

recipes.title: Easy garlicky Swiss chard
steps: Rinse the chard well. Cut the thick stems out and chop them into 1-inch pieces. Chop the leaves.
Warm the oil with the garlic, chili flakes and coriander seeds for about 30 seconds.
Add the stems, cover, and cook on low 3–4 minutes.
Add the leaves, toss, cover and cook 3–4 minutes more until wilted. Add salt if you like.
recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days in the fridge.
recipes.variety: Bright Lights or Fordhook Giant — colorful stems look great.

photo.by: Xufanc. Close-equivalent photo: shows chard sautéed with garlic and leeks (Catalan style)

recipes.title: Quick roasted beet cubes
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a pan with parchment.
Toss the beet cubes with oil and thyme.
Spread them out and sprinkle with salt.
Roast 10–20 minutes until a fork slides in easily.
recipes.storage: Keeps 5 days in the fridge — great in salads.
recipes.variety: Detroit Dark Red or golden beets (golden ones do not stain).

photo.note: Representative photo – not from the recipe page

recipes.title: Kettle corn
steps: Heat the oil in a big pot over medium heat.
Stir in the kernels and sugar, then cover.
Shake the pot the whole time so the sugar does not burn. When pops slow to one every 2–3 seconds, take it off the heat and keep shaking a few seconds.
Pour into a big bowl and stir now and then as it cools to break up clumps. Careful — melted sugar is very hot.
recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days in a sealed bag.
recipes.variety: Hulless popcorn types; dry the ears well and test-pop first.

src.t: NCHFP — Drying popcorn

photo.note: Representative photo – not from the recipe page

recipes.title: Sweet corn chowder
steps: Melt the butter with the bacon in a big pot. Add onion, pepper, carrot and celery and cook gently 5 minutes.
Break the bare cobs in half and add them with the milk and bay leaf. Bring just to a boil, then simmer gently 20 minutes (the cobs add sweet corn flavor).
Add potatoes, salt and thyme. Simmer about 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Take out the cobs, bacon and bay leaf. Add the corn kernels and pepper and simmer 5 minutes more.
recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days in the fridge. Do not boil hard when reheating.
recipes.variety: Super-sweet corn picked the same day.

crops.amt: 4–5 ears (about 3 cups kernels) — keep the cobs!

photo.note: Representative photo – not from the recipe page

recipes.title: Grilled corn caprese salad
steps: Grill the corn in its husks over high heat about 15 minutes, turning often. Cool, husk, and cut off the kernels.
Whisk oil, vinegar, salt, pepper (and sugar if the corn is not very sweet).
Toss corn, tomatoes, green onions, mozzarella and dressing. Let it sit 10 minutes.
Stir in the basil just before serving.
recipes.storage: Keeps 1 day in the fridge (add basil fresh).
recipes.variety: Sungold cherry tomatoes and any sweet corn.

crops.amt: 3 cups chopped or halved cherry tomatoes

recipes.title: Easy 5-minute cucumber salad
steps: Peel thick-skinned cucumbers (thin-skinned ones can stay unpeeled). Scoop out seeds only if they are big and tough.
Slice the cucumbers thin.
Toss with rice vinegar, herbs, salt and pepper.
Eat now, or chill up to a couple of hours.
recipes.storage: Best the same day.
recipes.variety: Any slicing cucumber; Persian types need no peeling.
recipes.kid: A first knife-skills recipe (with a grown-up).

photo.note: Representative photo – not from the recipe page

recipes.title: Spiced pumpkin bread
steps: Homemade purée: halve a small sugar pumpkin, scoop out the seeds (roast them!), bake cut-side down at 350°F until soft, then scoop and mash.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and butter a 4x8 loaf pan. Whisk flour, salt, soda and spices.
In another bowl mix pumpkin, sugar, butter, eggs, water, molasses and zest. Stir in the dry mix just until no flour shows. Add nuts.
Bake 45–60 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool 5 minutes, then turn out. Drizzle glaze if you like.
recipes.storage: Keeps 4 days wrapped; freezes 3 months.
recipes.variety: Small sugar pie pumpkins (New England Pie, Small Sugar) — not jack-o-lanterns.

crops.amt: 1 cup purée (roast a small sugar pumpkin, or use canned)

src.t: NCHFP — Pumpkin seeds (drying and roasting)

recipes.title: Zucchini spice muffins
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a 12-cup muffin pan.
Beat the eggs with sugar and vanilla. Stir in the zucchini and melted butter.
Mix flour, soda, powder, spices and salt, then stir into the zucchini mix — do not over-mix. Fold in nuts or raisins.
Fill the cups to the top and bake 22–30 minutes until golden and springy.
recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days; freezes 3 months.
recipes.variety: Use extra-big zucchini; no need to peel.

photo.note: Representative photo – not from the recipe page

recipes.title: Sweet potato biscuits
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Mix flour, baking powder, sugar and salt. Rub in the shortening until the bits are pea-size.
Stir in the mashed sweet potato and milk to make a soft dough. Pat it 1/2 inch thick on a floured counter and cut rounds with a glass.
Bake 1 inch apart for 12–15 minutes until golden.
recipes.storage: Best warm; keep 2 days in a sealed bag or freeze.
recipes.variety: Any orange sweet potato; leftover baked ones are perfect.
recipes.kid: Kids can cut the biscuits.

recipes.title: Green tomato spice cake
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease and flour a 9x13 pan.
Toss the green tomatoes with 1 Tbsp salt and wait 10 minutes. Rinse in cold water and drain well.
Beat butter and sugar until fluffy, then beat in the eggs one at a time. Mix flour, spices, soda and 1/4 tsp salt with the raisins and nuts, and stir it in.
Fold in the tomatoes, spread in the pan, and bake 40–45 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
recipes.storage: Keeps 4 days covered; freezes well.
recipes.variety: Any firm green tomatoes picked before the first frost.

crops.amt: 4 cups chopped GREEN (unripe) tomatoes — end-of-season fruit

recipes.title: Green tomato chutney (fridge & freezer)
steps: Core and chop the green tomatoes.
Put everything in a heavy 4-quart pot. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 45 minutes.
Uncover and simmer, stirring, until thick and jammy. Take out the cinnamon stick.
Spoon into clean jars, cool, and refrigerate or freeze. (This is not a USDA-tested canning recipe, so do not store it on the shelf.)
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 1 month; freezer up to 1 year (leave 1/2 inch space in jars).
recipes.variety: Use the green tomatoes left on the vines before frost.

crops.amt: 2 1/2 lb firm GREEN tomatoes (about 7 cups chopped)

recipes.title: Fresh creamed corn
steps: Cut the kernels off the cobs. Then scrape each bare cob with the back of the knife to catch the sweet "milk".
Melt the butter and cook the onion 3–4 minutes until soft.
Add the corn, its milk, salt, pepper and half and half. Simmer, stirring, until thick and creamy, about 8–10 minutes.
Top with chopped herbs.
recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
recipes.variety: Any sweet corn picked that morning.

photo.note: Representative photo of creamed corn – not from the recipe page

recipes.title: Strawberry rhubarb pie
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Mix rhubarb, strawberries, sugar, tapioca, salt and zest; let it sit 10 minutes.
Line a pie dish with one crust and pour in the filling.
Cover with the second crust, crimp the edges, brush the top and cut a few steam slits.
Bake 20 minutes at 400°F, then about 40–50 minutes at 350°F until the juices bubble. Cool well so the filling sets.
recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days at room temperature or 4 days in the fridge.
recipes.variety: Red-stalked Canada Red or Valentine rhubarb; June-bearing berries.

crops.amt: 3 1/2 cups stalks in 1/2-inch pieces (stalks only — leaves are poisonous)

photo.note: Representative photo – not from the recipe page

recipes.title: Classic sweet potato pie
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Halve the sweet potatoes, poke them, and roast cut-side down on parchment 45–50 minutes until very soft (bake the pie shell alongside until lightly golden).
Peel off the skins and whisk the warm flesh smooth.
Whisk in eggs one at a time, then sugar, spices, salt, butter and half and half.
Pour into the shell and bake at 350°F (175°C) 45–55 minutes, until the edges puff and the center barely jiggles. Cool on a rack.
recipes.storage: Keeps 4 days in the fridge.
recipes.variety: Deep-orange sweet potatoes like Beauregard.

photo.note: Representative photo – not from the recipe page

recipes.title: Simple coleslaw
steps: If using vinegar, stir it into the mayonnaise.
Slice or shred the cabbage as thin or chunky as you like.
Mix cabbage and onion (and carrot) with the dressing in a big bowl.
Let it rest at least 20 minutes — a couple of hours is even better.
recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
recipes.variety: Dense heads like Early Jersey Wakefield or Copenhagen Market.

recipes.title: Maple pumpkin pie
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
Blend everything except the pie shell into a smooth filling.
Pour it into the unbaked shell.
Bake 45 minutes. Cool before slicing.
recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
recipes.variety: Sugar pie pumpkins or butternut squash make silky purée.

photo.note: Photo from the Wikibooks recipe page

recipes.title: Fried green tomatoes
steps: Slice the tomatoes 1/4–1/2 inch thick.
Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Press each slice into cornmeal and fry in hot oil over medium heat about 3 minutes until golden underneath.
Flip gently and fry the other side. Serve hot, maybe with a little goat cheese.
recipes.storage: Best hot from the pan.
recipes.variety: Any firm, full-size green tomato.

crops.amt: 1 cup cornmeal from your own dry corn

recipes.title: Bread-and-butter pickles (USDA tested)
steps: Wash cucumbers, cut 1/16 inch off the blossom end, and slice 3/16 inch thick. Mix with the onions and salt, cover with 2 inches of crushed or cubed ice, and refrigerate 3–4 hours (add ice as needed). Drain well.
Boil the vinegar, sugar and spices in a large pot for 10 minutes.
Add the cucumbers and onions and slowly reheat to boiling. Fill jars with slices and syrup, leaving 1/2-inch headspace. Wipe rims, put on lids.

Process times are for 0–1,000 ft elevation; process pints or quarts 10 min in a boiling-water canner (1,001–6,000 ft: 15 min; above 6,000 ft: 20 min). Store 4–5 weeks for the best flavor. Follow the full USDA recipe.
recipes.storage: Sealed jars: cool, dark place, best within 1 year. Refrigerate after opening.
recipes.variety: Pickling cucumbers 4–5 inches long, or slender squash (do not use the lime variation with squash).

crops.amt: 6 lb of 4- to 5-inch pickling cucumbers (or slender zucchini / yellow squash)

recipes.title: Pickled beets (USDA tested)
steps: Trim the tops, leaving 1 inch of stem and the root so the color does not bleed. Wash, sort by size, cover with boiling water and cook until tender (25–30 minutes). Drain and throw away the liquid.
Cool, trim, and slip off the skins. Slice 1/4 inch thick. Peel and thinly slice the onions.

Bring vinegar, salt, sugar and fresh water to a boil with the spices tied in cheesecloth. Add beets and onions and simmer 5 minutes. Remove the spice bag. Fill jars with beets and onions, then hot liquid, leaving 1/2-inch headspace.
Process times are for 0–1,000 ft elevation; process pints or quarts 30 min in a boiling-water canner (1,001–3,000 ft: 35; 3,001–6,000 ft: 40; above 6,000 ft: 45 min). Follow the full USDA recipe.
recipes.storage: Sealed jars: cool, dark place, best within 1 year.
recipes.variety: Detroit Dark Red; baby beets (1–1 1/2 inch) can be packed whole.

recipes.title: Pickled corn relish (USDA tested)

Simmer peppers, celery, onions, sugar, vinegar, salt and celery seed for 5 minutes, stirring now and then.

Mix the mustard and turmeric into 1/2 cup of the hot liquid, then stir it and the corn into the pot. Simmer 5 minutes more (thicken with the flour paste if you like). Fill jars, leaving 1/2-inch headspace.
Process times are for 0–1,000 ft elevation; process half-pints or pints 15 min in a boiling-water canner (1,001–6,000 ft: 20; above 6,000 ft: 25 min). Follow the full USDA recipe.

recipes.title: Corncob jelly (NCHFP tested)
steps: Wash the cobs, cut them into 4-inch pieces, cover with 2 quarts water and boil slowly 35–40 minutes. Strain through a jelly bag or double cheesecloth without squeezing.
Sterilize the jars. Measure 3 cups of the juice (add water if short), stir in the pectin and bring to a boil.
Add all the sugar at once, return to a full rolling boil while stirring, and boil 5 minutes. Skim the foam. Fill jars leaving 1/4-inch headspace.
Process times are for 0–1,000 ft elevation; process half-pints or pints 5 min in a boiling-water canner (1,001–6,000 ft: 10; above 6,000 ft: 15 min). Follow the full NCHFP recipe.
recipes.storage: Sealed jars: cool, dark place, best within 1 year.
recipes.variety: Red-cobbed field (dent) corn like Bloody Butcher gives a pink jelly.

recipes.title: Lord Woolton pie (1941)
steps: Put the vegetables, oats and vegetable extract in a pot with just enough water to cover. Simmer 10 minutes, stirring so nothing sticks.
Let it cool, then spoon into a pie dish and sprinkle with parsley.
Cover with a pastry or mashed-potato crust.
Bake at about 375°F (190°C) until the crust is browned, 30–40 minutes. Serve with gravy.
recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
recipes.variety: Whatever winter roots you have — that was the point in 1941.

recipes.title: Carrot & potato croquettes (WWII)
steps: Mix the grated carrot, potato and cheese.
Season with salt, pepper and mustard. Stir in the oats to make a firm mix.
Shape into small logs or patties.
Fry in a little hot oil until golden and cooked through, about 4 minutes per side.
recipes.storage: Best fresh; reheat in the oven.
recipes.variety: Any storage carrot (Danvers, Chantenay).

recipes.title: Steamed chocolate carrot pudding (WWII)
steps: Cream the margarine and sugar.
Stir in the carrot, syrup and all the dry ingredients.
Add milk to make a fairly stiff batter.
Spoon into a greased heatproof bowl, cover with foil, and steam (bowl in a pot of simmering water, lid on) for 2 hours. Top up the water as needed.
recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days wrapped; reheat by steaming or microwave.
recipes.variety: Sweet carrots like Scarlet Nantes.

recipes.title: Wartime carrot cookies
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Grease a baking tray.
Beat the margarine and sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in the vanilla and carrot.
Fold in the flour, adding the water if the dough is dry.
Drop spoonfuls on the tray, sprinkle with a little sugar, and bake about 20 minutes. Makes 12–15 small cookies.
recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days in a tin.
recipes.variety: Any carrot — even the twisted ones.

recipes.title: Pathfinder pudding (parsnip, leek & cheese)
steps: Mix flour, 1/2 tsp salt and baking powder. Add the suet, shredded potato and just enough water to make a dough.
Roll out three-quarters of it and line a greased 2-pint heatproof bowl.
Mix the parsnips, cheese, leek, mustard, pepper and 1 tsp salt. Pack it into the bowl and top with a lid of the remaining pastry.
Cover with foil and steam 2 hours in a covered pot of simmering water (top up the water).
recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
recipes.variety: Frost-sweetened parsnips (Harris Model, Hollow Crown).

recipes.title: Carrot-nut ring with lima beans (1940s)
steps: Heat the oven to 325°F (165°C). Grease a 9-inch ring pan (or a loaf pan).
Beat the eggs until thick, then mix in milk, pepper, salt, honey and lemon juice. Stir in the almonds and carrots.
Pour into the pan, set it in a bigger pan of hot water that comes halfway up, and bake about 40 minutes until set.
Turn it out onto a platter and fill the middle with the hot lima beans.
recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days in the fridge.
recipes.variety: Fordhook or Henderson baby limas.

crops.amt: 2 cups cooked baby limas, kept hot

recipes.title: Victory garden curried carrots
steps: Chop the carrots and boil or steam until just tender.
Meanwhile cook the onion in the margarine for a few minutes. Stir in the curry powder and flour for a couple more minutes.
Stir in the stock, bring to a boil, season, add the sugar and simmer gently 20 minutes.
Add the carrots and cook 10 minutes more. Sprinkle parsley; serve with rice.

recipes.variety: Any carrots; great for big storage carrots.

recipes.title: Wartime carrot cake
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C; 200°C fan). Line a small cake tin.
Sift the flour into a bowl and rub in the margarine with your fingertips.
Mix in the sugar, carrot, sultanas and egg, then enough milk to make a sticky batter.
Spread in the tin and bake 40–45 minutes until golden.
recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days in a tin.
recipes.variety: Sweet Nantes carrots.

recipes.title: Fresh basil pesto
steps: Put the basil and nuts in a food processor and pulse a few times.
Add the garlic and cheese and pulse again. Scrape the sides down with a spatula.
With the machine running, pour the oil in a thin, slow stream so it blends smooth.
Taste and add salt and pepper. Toss with pasta, spoon on potatoes, or spread on toast.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 3 days with a thin layer of oil on top. To keep it longer see "Freeze basil pesto". Garlic or herbs in oil must stay in the fridge — never leave it at room temperature.
recipes.variety: Genovese-type sweet basil, picked before it flowers.

recipes.title: Tomatillo salsa verde
steps: Pull the papery husks off the tomatillos and rinse off the sticky coating. Cut them in half.
Lay them cut-side down on a foil-lined pan (with garlic cloves in their skins, if using). Broil about 6 inches from the heat for 5–7 minutes, until the skins blacken in spots.
No broiler? Sear them in a hot oiled skillet on both sides, or simmer them in water for 5 minutes.
Blend the tomatillos with the lime juice, onion, peeled garlic, cilantro and peppers until finely chopped. Salt to taste, cool, and chill.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to about 5 days. For shelf-stable salsa use a USDA-tested canning recipe only.
recipes.variety: Tomatillos are their own plant (grow 2+ for pollination); any jalapeño or serrano.

recipes.title: Green goddess herb dressing
steps: Wash and dry the herbs well, then chop them.
Put everything in a blender or food processor.
Blend 30–45 seconds until smooth and pale green.
Use it as a dip for raw garden veggies or toss it with lettuce.
recipes.storage: Keeps about a week in the fridge.
recipes.variety: Flat-leaf parsley and any chives; French tarragon if you grow it.
recipes.kid: Kids can snip the chives with scissors.

recipes.title: Jalapeño hot sauce
steps: Wear gloves when you slice the peppers, and keep your hands away from your eyes.
In a glass or enamel pan, cook the oil, peppers, garlic, onion and salt over high heat for 4 minutes. Add the water and cook 20 minutes, stirring often.
Let it cool to room temperature, then purée it smooth. Keep the blender running and slowly pour in the vinegar.
Pour into a very clean jar with a tight lid and keep it in the fridge.
recipes.storage: Fridge only — the source says it keeps up to 6 months refrigerated. This is not a tested canning recipe, so never store it on the shelf.
recipes.variety: Fully grown green jalapeños; red ones make it sweeter.

recipes.title: Garden marinara sauce
steps: Peel the tomatoes: dip them in boiling water for about a minute, cool them in ice water, and slip the skins off. Crush them with your hands.
Warm the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion and garlic about 2 minutes, until the onion looks clear.
Add the thyme, basil and bell pepper and cook 5 more minutes.
Add the tomatoes and sugar. Bring to a boil, then turn it down and simmer gently for 30 minutes, stirring now and then.
Salt to taste and spoon over pasta, rice or fish.
recipes.storage: Fridge up to 4 days, or freeze. To can tomato sauce, use only the NCHFP tested tomato recipes (with added acid).
recipes.variety: Roma, San Marzano or Amish Paste tomatoes cook down thick.

recipes.title: Tzatziki cucumber yogurt sauce
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a strainer lined with cheesecloth or a coffee filter and let it drip for about 3 hours, so it gets thick.
Salt the diced cucumber and let it drain too, then pat it dry.
Stir the thick yogurt with the garlic, oil and lemon juice. Cover and chill at least 1 hour.
Whisk in the dill and cucumber, then add salt and pepper to taste.
recipes.storage: Keeps 3–4 days in the fridge.
recipes.variety: Small pickling or Persian cucumbers have fewer seeds.

recipes.title: Rich vegetable stock

recipes.title: Apple barbecue sauce
steps: Stir everything together in a large saucepan.
Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then let it bubble down until you have about 4 cups.
Cool and pour into a jar or squeeze bottle for grilling and dipping.
recipes.storage: Keeps up to 3 weeks in the fridge. Not a tested canning recipe.
recipes.variety: Use your own apple jelly and ketchup if you made them.

crops.amt: 4 cups ketchup (see the tested tomato ketchup recipe)
chipotle hot sauce is smoked jalapeño

recipes.title: Teriyaki sauce & marinade
steps: Put everything in a small pot over low heat.
Stir just until the sugar melts — no need to boil.
Cool, then marinate meat, tofu or vegetables in it overnight in the fridge.
recipes.storage: Keeps about a week in the fridge. Garlic in liquid must stay in the fridge.
recipes.variety: Homegrown ginger: dig a piece from the side of the pot.

crops.amt: 1 tsp fresh, peeled and finely chopped

recipes.title: Beef stock (white or brown)
steps: For brown stock, first roast the bones at 400°F, turning them, until well browned; brown the onion and carrot in the roasting pan, and rinse the pan out with a little water into the pot. For white stock, skip this.
Cover the bones with water by 2 inches. Heat slowly to a simmer, skimming off the foam, then keep it just simmering (never boiling) for 30 minutes.
Skim again, add the vegetables, herbs tied in a bundle, peppercorns and salt. Partly cover and simmer 6–8 hours.
Lift out the bones, strain through cheesecloth, cool fast in a sink of cold water and chill. Lift off the hard fat and freeze in portions.
recipes.storage: Cool it fast, then keep it in the fridge a few days or freeze it in portions. Canning stock needs a pressure canner and a tested process — see Preserve & Store.
recipes.variety: Big storage onions and the leeks you are clearing from the bed.

crops.amt: 2, with the green part, washed well

recipes.title: Kale & garlic linguine
steps: Melt the butter into the oil in a big skillet. Add the garlic and chile flakes and cook gently until the garlic is soft but not brown.

Boil the kale in a big pot of well-salted water about 4 minutes, until bright green. Lift it into the skillet with a slotted spoon (keep the water) and cook, stirring, until dark, soft and nearly dry.
Cook the linguine in the same water until just tender, then move it into the skillet with tongs.
Toss with the greens and the parmesan until glossy. Serve hot.
recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days in the fridge.
recipes.variety: Lacinato or curly kale — sweeter after frost.

crops.amt: 1–2 bunches, stems removed, cut in bite-size pieces

recipes.title: Cabbage rolls in tomato sauce (holubtsi)
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Soften the cabbage leaves in a covered pot of boiling water for 3 minutes, then drain.
Mix the beef, rice, egg, milk, onion, salt and pepper and split it into 12 parts. Wrap each in a leaf, pin with a toothpick, and set them in a baking dish.
Stir the tomato paste, tomatoes, 1/2 cup water, vinegar and sugar together, pour it over the rolls, cover, and bake 40 minutes.
Move the rolls to a platter and pull the toothpicks. Thicken the sauce with the cornstarch stirred into 1/2 cup cold water, warming it if needed, and spoon it over.
recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; freezes well.
recipes.variety: Big outer leaves from a loose cabbage head; savoy rolls easily.

crops.amt: 1 can (or about 2 cups) chopped tomatoes + 1 can tomato paste

recipes.title: Acorn squash with orange marmalade
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (204°C). Scrape out the seeds and strings and trim a thin slice off the back of each half so it sits flat.
Set the halves cut-side down in a shallow dish with 1/4 inch of water and bake 35 minutes.
Flip them over and salt lightly. Mix the marmalade and butter and spread it over the cut edges so it runs into the hollow.
Slide under the broiler about 5 minutes, until lightly browned.
recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
recipes.variety: Acorn squash (no curing needed — eat within a couple of months).

recipes.title: Apple & parsnip soup
steps: Chop the onion and cook it in the oil until golden.
Chop the apples, carrot and parsnip and add them with the water, nutmeg, lemon juice and soup mix if using.
Simmer about an hour, until the carrot is very soft.
Blend until completely smooth. Serve hot or cold.
recipes.storage: Keeps 4 days in the fridge; freezes well.
recipes.variety: Parsnips dug after frost are sweetest.

recipes.title: Spiced pumpkin & sweet potato soup
steps: Melt the butter in a large pot and cook the onion 3–4 minutes. Stir in the flour, curry, cumin, nutmeg and garlic for 1 minute.
Add the sweet potato, salt, stock and pumpkin. Bring to a boil, then partly cover and simmer 20–25 minutes until the sweet potato is soft. Rest 10 minutes.
Blend in batches until smooth and pour back through a strainer.
Stir in the milk and heat 5 minutes over medium. Off the heat, add the lime juice.
recipes.storage: Keeps 4 days in the fridge; freezes well (before adding the milk is best).
recipes.variety: Sugar pie pumpkins or butternut; any orange sweet potato.

recipes.title: Zuppa Toscana (sausage, potato & kale soup)
steps: Brown the sausage in a skillet, breaking it up, and drain. Brown the bacon and drain it too.
Simmer the water, broth, potatoes, garlic and onion in a big pot until the potatoes are tender.
Add the sausage and bacon and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in the kale or chard and the cream, season, and heat through.
recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days in the fridge (cream soups don’t freeze well).
recipes.variety: Russet potatoes and a big handful of kale or chard.

recipes.title: Waldorf salad
steps: Cut the apples into wedges and toss them with the lemon juice so they stay white.
Soak the raisins in warm water 5 minutes and drain. Add them to the apples with the celery and walnuts.
Stir the mayonnaise and sugar together, fold it through lightly, and chill at least 30 minutes.
Serve on lettuce leaves, topped with cherries if you like.
recipes.storage: Best the same day.
recipes.variety: A tart green apple plus a sweet red one.

recipes.title: Curtido (spicy pickled cabbage slaw)
steps: Dunk the chopped cabbage in boiling water for a few seconds and drain.
Mix it with the other vegetables, oregano, vinegar or lime juice, a little water and salt in a glass or plastic container (stir with a wooden spoon).
Cover and refrigerate about a week so it turns tangy, then serve with pupusas, tacos or beans.
recipes.storage: Keeps several weeks in the fridge. A fridge pickle — not shelf-stable.
recipes.variety: Firm green cabbage; any carrots.

recipes.title: Pumpkin muffins
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and grease a muffin pan. Sift the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt and cinnamon together.
Beat the egg, then stir in the milk, pumpkin and oil.
Pour the wet mix into a well in the dry mix and stir just until no flour shows. Fill the cups two-thirds full.
Bake about 25 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Loosen with a spatula and serve warm.
recipes.storage: Keeps 2 days; freezes 3 months.
recipes.variety: Small sugar pie pumpkins or butternut squash.
recipes.kid: Kids can fill the muffin cups.

recipes.title: Savory pumpkin scones
steps: Heat the oven to 430°F (220°C). Stir the flour, milk powder, spring onion and nutmeg together.
Gently fold in the pumpkin, buttermilk and water to make a soft dough.
Pat it out on a floured board about 5/8 inch thick and cut 12 rounds with a 2-inch cutter.
Bake on a floured tray 12–15 minutes until golden. Serve with butter or cottage cheese.
recipes.storage: Best the same day; freeze extras.
recipes.variety: Leftover roasted pumpkin or squash.

recipes.title: Apple crisp
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Mix the flour, brown sugar, oats and cinnamon (chill it if your kitchen is warm).
Slice the apples into a 9-inch square baking dish — glass works best.
Quickly cut the cold butter into the topping in small bits (two knives, scissor-style) so it doesn’t melt, then scatter it over the apples and pat lightly.
Bake about 30 minutes, until the top is deep brown and the apples bubble.
recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days covered.
recipes.variety: Firm baking apples that hold their shape.
recipes.kid: Kids can sprinkle the topping.

recipes.title: Spiced apple cake
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (177°C) and grease and line a cake pan.
Beat the butter and sugar until fluffy, then beat in the eggs.
Sift the flour, soda and spices and stir them in just until mixed. Fold in the apples.
Spread in the pan and bake about 45 minutes. Serve warm with whipped cream.
recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days covered.
recipes.variety: Any apples — a mix is nice.

recipes.title: Leek, potato & herb vegetable stock
steps: Trim the leeks, cut them in 1-inch pieces, soak them in a bowl of water, and lift them out so the grit stays behind.
Wash and cut the other vegetables in 1-inch chunks (onion and garlic skins can go in, but not the onion root).
Put everything in a stockpot with cold water just to cover. Bring to a boil, then keep it at the barest simmer for 1 hour.
Strain into another pot (through cheesecloth for a clear stock). Boil it down further for a stronger flavor if you like.
recipes.storage: Cool it fast, then keep it in the fridge a few days or freeze it in portions. Canning stock needs a pressure canner and a tested process — see Preserve & Store.
recipes.variety: Leeks, carrots, celery and herbs straight from the fall garden.

recipes.title: Simple garden herb broth
steps: Bring 6 cups of water to a boil.
Add the cut-up leeks, onion and scallions, all the herbs, and some salt and pepper.
Cook over medium heat about 2 hours, stirring now and then and adding water if it gets low.
Strain out the herbs and vegetables. Sip it, or use it as stock.
